title: Protocols and Enforcement Measures for Oversight of Retrenchments
what_it_is: Protocols and Enforcement Measures for Oversight of Retrenchments

sections.label: Retrenchment questions to Manpower Minister
sections.summary: Questions ask about union notice, MRN timing, retrenched workers' incomes, enforcement, and pro-enterprise tripartite practices.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower in respect of a recent retrenchment exercise by a multinational technology company with a global headquarters in Singapore (a) whether the Ministry will look into how the relevant union was informed only a day in advance; (b) when was the Ministry notified of the retrenchment; (c) whether the retrenched workers' incomes are within the broad middle-income range in Singapore; and (d) how can Singapore continue to be pro-enterprise and attract investment while maintaining tripartite best practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower in light of the recent retrenchment exercise by a multinational technology company with its headquarters in Singapore (a) whether the Ministry will review and strengthen current protocols to better manage future retrenchments, including ensuring that unions are given more timely notice beyond just one day; and (b) what steps is the Ministry taking to enhance pro-worker guidelines that can simultaneously encourage multinational companies to maintain their presence in Singapore while safeguarding the welfare of workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower in light of recent retrenchments by MNCs which involve professionals, managers and executives (PMEs) being laid off (a) whether the Ministry can take tougher enforcement action against companies that fail to comply with the tripartite advisories and guidelines on retrenchment of workers including PMEs; and (b) whether the Ministry can look into ensuring that companies notify the unions early in advance of impending retrenchments to allow for discussions, negotiations and pre-emptive assistance for affected workers and members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) for each year from 2019 to date in 2024, what is the number of companies that failed to file a mandatory retrenchment notification (MRN) within the requisite period; (b) whether the Ministry will consider reviewing the existing exemptions from MRN; and (c) whether the Ministry will consider reviewing the MRN period to require MRNs to be submitted prior to retrenchment instead of post-retrenchment.

sections.label: Dyson retrenchment and collective agreement
sections.summary: PMEs are outside the union's collective representation, so notice period is negotiable and Dyson followed laws and tripartite advisories.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Thus, they are not within the scope of the union’s collective representation and the period of notice is therefore negotiable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Hence, Dyson handled the recent retrenchment exercise in accordance with our laws and tripartite advisories, as the PMEs are not under the collective agreement.

sections.label: Retrenchment benefit quantum norms
sections.summary: Prevailing norm is two weeks to one month salary per year of service, and Dyson's PME benefit aligned with the Tripartite Advisory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: The prevailing norm is between two weeks to one month salary per year of service, and the retrenchment payments depend on the financial position of the company and industry norms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: While there is no requirement to do so and the affected workers are not covered by collective agreement, Dyson provided a retrenchment benefit quantum for its PMEs that is in line with our Tripartite Advisory.

sections.label: Late mandatory retrenchment notifications
sections.summary: From 2019 to March 2024, about 30% of MRNs were submitted late, after five working days of notifying affected employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: In response to the question from a Member on the MRNs submitted from 2019 to March 2024, about 30% of MRNs were submitted late, after five working days of notifying the affected employees.

sections.label: Small employer MRN exemption
sections.summary: Employers with less than 10 employees are exempted from MRNs, an agreed tripartite position, though early notification is encouraged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Currently, employers with less than 10 employees are exempted from submitting MRNs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: This is an agreed tripartite position, given that it may place too much administrative burden to make smaller companies submit MRNs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Nonetheless, we encourage all employers to notify MOM of any retrenchment exercise early, so that we can extend support to the affected employees.

sections.label: TAFEP engagement on tripartite advisory
sections.summary: If an employer does not follow the tripartite advisory, TAFEP will engage the employer to adhere to it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: If an employer does not follow the tripartite advisory, the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices, or TAFEP, will engage the employer to adhere to it.

sections.label: MOM unfair employment practices enforcement
sections.summary: MOM will investigate unfair employment practices and take enforcement action as needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: MOM will also investigate unfair employment practices and take enforcement action as needed.

sections.label: Government tripartite worker support ecosystem
sections.summary: The Government works with tripartite partners to support workers throughout their careers, without waiting for retrenchments.

sentences.text: At the same time, what I can assure Members is this: we do not wait for retrenchments to happen before we help workers.

The Government has worked closely with our tripartite partners, the unions, the employers, to develop an ecosystem that supports workers on every step of their career journey, even during disruptions.

sections.label: Retrenched residents reemployed within six months
sections.summary: In the second quarter of 2024, more than half of retrenched residents secured jobs within six months of retrenchment.

sentences.text: In the second quarter of 2024, more than half of all retrenched residents were able to find and secure jobs within six months of being retrenched.

sections.label: Dyson retrenchment benefits for affected workers
sections.summary: Dyson provided retrenchment benefits to all affected workers even though they are not covered by collective agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: As I have shared, on the Dyson case, for example, they have provided retrenchment benefits to all affected workers, even though they are not covered by collective agreement.

sections.label: Retrenched workers find jobs within six months
sections.summary: Most retrenched workers find job opportunities within six months, which the speaker calls a good space.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: So, we are in a good space at this moment in time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Therefore, you find that most of the workers who have been retrenched do find job opportunities within six months.

sections.label: Early notification mobilises retrenchment task force
sections.summary: Early notification allows mobilisation of the retrenchment task force, NTUC and Workforce Singapore teams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: One of the reasons why we hope to have early notification is so that we can mobilise the retrenchment task force, get the NTUC moving, get the Workforce Singapore teams moving to facilitate that.

sections.label: Review of retrenchment advisories and laws
sections.summary: MP asks if MOM can work with tripartite partners to review advisories, guidelines, regulations and employment laws before the next major retrenchment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: My supplementary question is, in light of these latest development of retrenchments in Singapore, which will impact workers including PMEs, can MOM work with tripartite partners to seriously review the various Tripartite Advisories, guidelines, regulations, employment and industrial relations laws, so that some of these ambiguities and lacunae can be addressed well before the next major retrenchment happens in Singapore?

sections.label: Openness to tripartite conversations
sections.summary: Speaker says there is room for improvement, tripartism needs trust and confidence, and they are open to conversations on laws, regulations or advisories.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: So, we have the perspectives from MOM, from the Labour Movement and employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: But in this case, I do agree that there is always room for improvement and tripartism has to be built based on trust and confidence; and certainly, both the workers and the employers want win-win outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Whether it is the laws, regulations or advisories, I think we are certainly open to have those conversations.
